files.name: 2026-09-06.md

frontmatter.title: Jots stopped belonging to the account

files.body:
Two commits finishing the move of Jots from account scope to project scope, and the ugly bug that
move exposed: switching projects silently threw away whatever you typed next.

Phase 1 landed last night — Jots now live under a project instead of the account. This morning was
the fallout. `JotsWorkspace` re-subscribed when you changed project but never cleared the selected
jot id, so a stale id from the old project sat there blocking auto-select. The old project's note
stayed on screen under the new project's name, and the next autosave went to the wrong address:
project B, jot id from project A. In mock mode that write is quietly discarded. In live mode it's
rejected. Either way your typing is gone and nothing tells you.

The fix resets the active jot on project change and cancels any autosave debounce still in flight,
but the part I care about is that the "what should be selected" rule moved out of the component into
`jotSelection.ts`, with tests. It's a rule with an obvious trap in it — two projects can coincidentally
have a jot with the same id, and the old code would have trusted that. That's not something I want
living inside a 1000-line workspace component where nobody can see it.

Same commit, a smaller thing that had been bothering me: creating a project dropped you on a blank
workspace. Now creating a project — desktop, mobile, or the default one made at first sign-in —
seeds the starter jots and lands you on the Jots tab with the Read Me open. A blank page is a
question the app should answer, not ask.

Then Phase 3: the migration modal for anyone with legacy account-level jots. Ask-once, mandatory,
pick which project the old notes belong to, copy them in with re-based order, seed starter jots into
every other project, mark it done. The decision logic sits behind a pure module so the
"nothing to migrate, complete yourself" path is testable without a DOM.

Also swept up three bits of drift the scope move left behind: two stale "existing account" comments,
and the Add Starter Jots buttons being clickable with no active project when the handler flatly
requires one.

Nothing released yet — these are phase commits.

Last thing today, and the reason this file exists at all: I set up the daily log. From here every
session writes the day's entry in `log/` **as the work happens**, not at the end — every fix,
feature, bug, phase commit, worker hand-off and release, shipped or not. These files get consumed
by the aggregator I'm building, so a missing entry is a missing published page rather than a
missing note. The rules are in CLAUDE.md and in the master session brief, so a fresh session picks
them up without me repeating myself, and the frozen format contract sits in `log/_format.md` where
the aggregator ignores it.

One correction to myself: I asked for `logs/`. The contract says `log/`. The contract wins.
